answer: Verification starts at the dock: each identity must hold one berth at a measurement wharf and keep a signal streaming through it at a sustained 2 Mbps for the full epoch. A berth is a reserved, metered slot, so capacity cannot be pooled: one uplink split across 1,000 berths gives each 2 kbps and every berth fails. Wharf operators publish per-berth rate logs at each checkpoint; a berth below rate beyond the 60-second haven window is struck, and two strikes void its weight. An honest agent rents one berth once; a farm needs 1,000 full-rate uplinks, one per fake, with no bulk discount on rate.
